summary: Closed the loop on the healed-partition fact by correcting it to the retained receipt's actual operands: the flag-enabled case ended with the restarted side as the single Leader at term 4 while the other side's committed entry was still in its store, and the flag-disabled control ended with the restarted side a follower at term 3 and a single entry — the earlier wording had the direction backwards, taken from construction-time feedback rather than from the receipt. The corrected entry keeps the substantive claim intact (one leader after healing while both divergent committed entries remain, the two having been written at the same index and term so each side treats the other as a duplicate rather than a conflict) and records that the post-heal winning side varied between local feedback and the retained run, so the surviving divergence does not depend on that direction; the controller accepts no explicit affected uses for that entry, so the change rests on the stated premise correction alone. Nothing else changed: the question remains explained, the defect claim asserted, no gaps open, and the account's claims all cite their receipts, with disk-backed stores, crash and restart timing, and further repetitions or longer runs remaining as recorded limitations rather than as open questions.
